title: What Is a Mention in AI Search?
description: A mention is when an AI engine names your brand or product without a link or a formal source credit. Here's how that's different from a citation.
focusKeyword: what is a mention in AI search
bodyMarkdown:
Quick answer

A mention is when an AI engine brings up your brand, product or name inside an answer, without formally crediting a specific page as the source. It's looser than a citation: no link, no footnote, sometimes not even full confidence that the AI got the details right. Mentions still matter, but they're a different signal than a citation.

Key takeaways
  • A mention names your brand, product or person without a formal source link behind it.
  • A citation is stricter: a specific page, credited as the source of a specific fact.
  • Mentions often come from training data (what the model learned in general), while citations usually come from a live crawl of a specific page.
  • You can influence mentions indirectly, by building a consistent, factual presence across the web, even though there's no single page to "optimize" for a mention.
Say someone asks ChatGPT "what are some good AEO audit tools?" and the answer says "tools like AI Page Audit can help you check this." That's a mention. No link, no specific page credited, just the name coming up because the model has seen it associated with the topic. ## How is a mention actually different from a citation? The difference comes down to attribution and source. | | Mention | Citation | |---|---|---| | Is there a link or footnote? | Usually no | Usually yes | | Is a specific page credited? | No, just a name | Yes, a specific URL | | Where does it usually come from? | The model's general training | A live crawl of your page, for this specific question | | Can you point to proof it happened? | Hard to verify after the fact | Often visible as a link right in the answer | Both are worth paying attention to, but for different reasons. A citation is a direct, checkable result tied to a specific page doing its job well. A mention is more like reputation: it reflects whether your brand shows up consistently enough, across enough of the web, that a model has learned to associate your name with the topic. [[chart:0]] ## Why does my brand get mentioned but never cited? This is common, and it usually means one of two things: 1. **Your brand has broad recognition, but your pages aren't structured for extraction.** The model "knows" your name from training data across many sources (reviews, forums, other articles about you), but when it needs to answer a specific question live, your own page isn't the easiest one to pull a clean quote from. 2. **Your content lives in places other than your own site.** If most of what's written about your brand is on third-party sites, forums or review platforms, the model may have learned your name from those, while your own website stays largely uncrawled or under-read for citations. > A mention tells you the model has heard of you. A citation tells you the model trusts your own page enough to quote it directly. Those are not the same achievement. ## Can I turn mentions into citations? Partially, yes. The fix is to make sure the facts people associate with your brand actually live on a page of yours that's easy for an AI crawler to read and quote. If you want to check whether your page is even visible to the crawlers that matter (GPTBot, PerplexityBot, ClaudeBot and others), the free LLM Access Check shows you exactly what each one sees. If a page looks fine to a human but keeps getting skipped, that's often the real reason, not a lack of reputation. ## Does a mention without a citation still help me? Yes, it still has value, just a different kind. It's closer to brand awareness than to the kind of direct traffic or authority signal a citation can carry. If you're building a strategy, it helps to track both separately rather than lumping them together. For the fuller picture of how AEO, SEO and GEO relate and where mentions and citations fit into each, see AEO vs SEO vs GEO. ## How do I know which one is actually happening for my brand? The only reliable way is to ask the AI engines directly about your topic and read the answers closely: is there a link next to the claim, or just a name? Doing this regularly, and pairing it with a structural check like the Full AEO & GEO Audit, gives you a much clearer picture than guessing from your search rankings alone, since mentions and citations don't show up in a normal analytics dashboard.

faqs.q: Is a mention better than nothing, even without a link?
faqs.a: Yes. It means the model associates your brand with the topic, which is a form of reach. It's just a weaker, less checkable signal than a citation.

faqs.q: Why does ChatGPT sometimes get details about my brand wrong in a mention?
faqs.a: Because a mention often comes from general training data rather than a live read of your current page, so it can reflect outdated or secondhand information instead of what's actually on your site today.

faqs.q: Can a mention turn into a bad outcome, like a wrong fact spreading?
faqs.a: Yes, this can happen, especially if the clearest, most current version of a fact about your brand isn't easy for AI crawlers to find on your own site. Making your own page the clearest source helps reduce this risk.

faqs.q: Do I need a certain amount of traffic to start getting mentioned?
faqs.a: Not traffic specifically, but you generally need enough presence across the web (your own site, reviews, press, forums) for a model to have learned your name in connection with the topic during training.

faqs.q: Is there a tool that tracks mentions the way rank trackers track SEO positions?
faqs.a: Not yet in the same standardized way SEO rank tracking exists. The practical approach today is manually asking AI engines about your topic and reading the answers, alongside a structural audit of your own pages.

faqs.q: Should I try to get mentions or citations first?
faqs.a: Citations are the more direct, controllable goal, since they come from your own page being read and trusted for a specific answer. Mentions tend to build up as a side effect of broader visibility over time.
